summary: Built the alt-step model: vertices S ⊆ {q_1..q_k}, label g(S)=Πq_i mod e; S~T is a certificate iff g(S)/g(T)=g(S∖T)/g(T∖S) ≡ −1, so the graph is a disjoint union of complete bipartite graphs K_{|c|,|−c|} between label classes c and −c. Hence the max certificate-free family is Σ_{pairs}max(|c|,|−c|) ≥ 2^{k−1} always, Huang's 2^{k−1}+1 size threshold forces nothing beyond 'some class c and −c both occupied', and 'an edge exists' is exactly the target-Davenport question already settled in BRAINSTORM/z33_target_davenport.md (η(G)>0 except exponent-2 levels t | 24). No signing of this graph carries χ-information beyond the label partition.

The matched random model and its criticality are already worked out: s9_janson_dependency.md measures E[#hit levels]=(0.44→0.97)·log p with level-Janson μ²/2Δ ≈ 0.85→1.82, and z45_critical_chaos.md §3.4 shows (PROVED bookkeeping) that mean ≠ no-hit hazard, that NL/L likely grows (≈0.061·L, crossing 1 near p≈1.4·10⁷) so 'critical' is not established, and gives the summability criterion for exp(−aμ^β) zero laws. Park–Pham adds nothing at fixed p (no product measure; technique_transfer_list §12); the expectation-threshold computation would only re-derive these first-moment numbers.

Computed E(N)=Σ_{n≤N}R(n)² to N=10⁸ (scripts/z52b_p1_H07_energy.c): E(N)/(N log⁴N) = 0.0178, 0.0167, 0.0164, 0.0163, 0.0162, 0.0161 for N=10³..10⁸, i.e. E ≍ N(log N)⁴ with E[R²]/E[R]² = 1.17 (all n) and 1.11 (primes ≡1 mod 4) at 10⁸, decaying like ≈1+2/log N. So the energy already sits at its Cauchy–Schwarz minimum (diagonal = mean²) up to 1+O(1/log N); no decoupling bound can improve it, and Chebyshev from it gives only exceptional density ≍ 1/log N, far weaker than Vaughan. Variance structure (genus split) is already in SINGLE_P_COUNT.md variance table.

Read GEOMETRY_ES Prop 2.1 (Looijenga pair = P² blown up at one point per side of the triangle, points collinear, D = cycle of three 0-curves, D² = 6, collinearity ⇒ a (−2)-curve contracted to the node) and checked the GHK/GHKS setup (arXiv:1106.4977, 1910.08427 verified). GHK theta functions give a canonical basis of regular functions on U_n (indexed by U^trop(ℤ), positive structure constants), but nothing in the machinery produces integral points: the flagship GHK example, Markoff-type cubics (mirror of the cubic surface, theta functions = trace functions), has infinitely many integral Hasse failures with non-empty BM set (Loughran–Mitankin arXiv:1807.10223, Ghosh–Sarnak), so 'positivity of theta structure constants ⇒ existence of integer points' is false in the closest case. Collinearity only places U_n at a special period point (the node); ES then remains the divisor event (rational_to_integral_cubic.md M2 already records the GHK-style degeneration analogy as B2).

KUDLA_ES.md already gives the full dictionary (T1 ⟺ oddness of Diff(T), Thms 1.2/1.4) and kills the Kudla route by Prop 2.4′: Kudla coefficients and deg Z(T) are functions of the genus of T, while genera mix certificate and non-certificate indices (582/2398 slices, p<3000); §3 item 4 already tried the unitary/CM base change (E = ℚ(ζ_M), Bruinier–Kudla–Yang/Howard–Yang η_{E/F}-incoherence) and found the moving modulus becomes a moving base field. Li–Zhang's theorem Int(L) = ∂Den(L) is by its very statement a local-density (hence genus) identity, so it lands in exactly the Prop 2.4′ obstruction; no new ES count appears as a cycle degree.

BRAINSTORM/y1_gamma8_trace.md Fact G2 already settles it: the word sign χ is not an SL₂(ℤ)-class function — M_(3,5,3) (n=37, χ=−1) and M_(5,3,3) (n=39, χ=+1) are conjugate hyperbolic matrices (trace 34), with 88 such pairs for letters ≤ 11 — and the memo explicitly lists 'linking number with the trefoil' among the excluded invariants. Ghys's Rademacher symbol Ψ is a conjugacy invariant, so it cannot determine the sign; Φ mod 12 is the eta-multiplier character (again a class function), and the sign is instead a Γ(8)-cell function (Fact G1).

Both cited memos already do exactly this: bsC_supersingular_transfer.md Thm 1/Cor 2 (PROVED) show the '∃ supersingular E' quantifier is vacuous — every certificate-shaped T has Diff(T)={p} and so lives on some supersingular curve — so curves add no condition; bsC_isogeny_ramanujan.md shows Type I = a pair of orthogonal isogenies with index condition e | a+b, that Pizer/Kane/Chevyrev–Galbraith degree existence needs degrees ≫ p^{2+ε} which Type I tuples never reach (R176 repair), and that walk mixing equidistributes endpoints, not the residue condition (B2/B3).

bsA_hecke_cusp_excursions.md H3 already gives the dictionary: r(p/A)−1 counts R-blocks of the Series cutting sequence of ∞→A/p, and λ(p) ≤ 3 is a three-excursion event of heights ≍ v,t,u with vtu ≍ p, of measure ≍ log²p/p — beyond any equidistribution/shrinking-target rate (B3/B6). y1_gamma8_trace.md counts the requested objects: three-letter Zagier/HJ cycles of trace T number ≤ #{abc−a−b−c=T} = O(T^{1/3+ε}), a T^{−2/3} fraction of the trace-formula count, and cycle length is not a spectral invariant; Pollicott/Lalley-type counts are over all classes of given length/trace, so they do not see the p-constraint (a matrix entry, not the trace).

The repo's screening checklist (FRONTIER §4 lines 1–3) is precisely the catalogue of 'fake ES' models with the right local statistics: (i) Type I/II counting at odd squares (T1) — all local, genus, spinor and BM conditions hold, the almost-all bound holds, yet failures are infinite (all m²); (ii) numerator 8, where Vaughan-type almost-all goes through but 8/131, 8/241 fail ((J)41, (J)86); (iii) fixed finite slice menus, which fail infinitely often under H ((I)8) or Dickson ((J)106, (J)83); plus the CRT/Cox surrogate models of z45_critical_chaos §3. The 'feature the fakes lack' is already distilled there (uses the quadratic character of p essentially, 4-specific/threshold, controls the class in a tied modulus). A fresh random-divisor fake would reproduce (iii)/z45.

Measured smoothness of C over all (★) solutions at 12 sample primes 10⁶–2·10⁹ (scripts/z52b_p1_H07_smoothC.py; R=0 confirmed at the 10 known (★)-failure primes 409…8813281): the fraction with P⁺(C) ≤ p^{0.1} is 0.27–0.58 (typ. ≈0.4) and with P⁺(C) ≤ log²p 0.65–0.92, slowly decreasing — exactly what a log-uniformly distributed C gives, so smooth-C restriction loses only a constant factor but carries no new structure. The theory side is already in tech_smooth_level.md: Drappeau/Harper/Zhang friable level-of-distribution results average over the integer (here 4Cp+1 or p), so at fixed p they are B6/H-A, and for the exceptional set smoothness only changes the constant below the structural 3/4 cap ((D)24).

WINDMILL.md and INVOLUTION_ES.md already did this comparison: INVOLUTION_ES §4 (R158 precursor note) reads Elsholtz 2010 §§2.1, 3 — Zagier-type maps for sx²+tyz are derived uniquely from k-independent coefficients + identical form invariance — and Lemma 4.1/Prop 4.2 show finite-menu fibre-preserving involutions on the ES sets reduce to identical invariance, whose AGL₄(ℤ) group on the Type II polynomial has order 4 (only a↔b survives on positive tuples, WINDMILL Prop 2); WINDMILL §2.4 finds divisor-class parity laws only for m | 24 and §3 tests ~7000 candidate weights with no generalising odd count (Jiang: ordered f_I, f_II even). The x²+ny² catalogue is exactly the 'special forms' for which Elsholtz's partitions close.

The points (a+i)/p are the Hecke points of bsA_hecke_cusp_excursions.md: H1 (QR/QNR = split-torus orbits on them), H2 (QNR half equidistributes, power saving), H3 (λ(p) ≤ 3 = the cusp-to-cusp geodesic ∞→A/p making ≤ 3 excursions of heights ≍ v,t,u with vtu ≍ p, an event of measure ≍ |L₃(p)|/p ≍ log²p/p). The memo already quantifies the scale gap the item asks for: even square-root-rate equidistribution misses a p^{−1+o(1)} cylinder by p^{1/2}, and Kleinbock–Margulis shrinking targets need measure ≫ (log p)^{−C}. Effective long-horocycle results (Strömbergsson, Sarnak) are of the same kind.

Already in the repo in the requested form: BRAINSTORM/y5_siegel_weil_chamber.md (PROVED) shows Siegel–Weil on full-rank data is just the genus indicator, the sign is the 2-adic genus label, and certificate (path-basis) lattices are a ≪ p^{−2/3+o(1)} fraction of the ≍ p classes in the ε₂ = −1 genus; the 'Eisenstein main term vs cusp error' gap is FRONTIER B3 (CONDITIONAL_ES Prop 2.3: main term must be ≤ p^{o(1)} for p^{o(1)}-to-one encodings, while cusp bounds need power-size main terms), and STRONG_APPROX_ES l.199 notes the cusp part is of the same size as the main term. KUDLA_ES Prop 2.4′ gives the same conclusion for the incoherent version.

Literature: arXiv:1108.6118 and 1606.02117 (verified) treat many-term odd/S-unit decompositions of 1, not three-term restricted 4/n, so no restricted three-term variants are tabulated there. Computation: all unordered solutions of 4/p for the 12 980 primes p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 3·10⁵ (scripts/z52b_p1_H07_allsol.c), then every allowed-class set S ⊂ ℤ/m, m ∈ {3,4,5,7,8} (scripts/z52b_p1_H07_restrict.py). Restrictions to multiples of k are just numerator 4k (all-even ⇔ 8/p: fails exactly at 17, 241 as known; all ≡0 mod 4 ⇔ 16/p: 31 fails to 83449; all ≡0 mod 3 ⇔ 12/p: 18 fails to 12241); every other non-parity-forbidden S that is large enough fails only at a few small primes (e.g. 3 ∤ xyz: only p = 241; no x ≡ 0,3 mod 4: only 181, 1009; mod 5 sets: last failure ≤ 2521), and no S fails on a whole residue class of p — so no new obstruction and no structurally distinguished strengthening.
